title: Waferscale Silicon Photonics Systems: A Cost-Benefit Analysis and Optimization
problem: Waferscale systems suffer from long-reach electrical interconnect overheads; silicon photonics offers potential but implementation costs and feasibility across topologies are unclear.
motivation: Quantifying silicon photonics benefits and overheads for waferscale enables informed architecture choices balancing latency reduction against power/area costs.
method: Analyzes tile-based silicon photonics waferscale systems across multiple waveguide implementations, topologies, and applications. Evaluates microring resonator power limits and custom waveguide networks.
key_novelty: First comprehensive analysis of silicon photonics vs. electrical interconnects at waferscale, identifying application-dependent benefits and topology-specific implementation challenges.
contributions: Performance comparison of silicon photonics vs. electrical interconnects at waferscale
Analysis showing benefits primarily from reduced communication latency
Identification of high power/area overheads, especially for high connectivity
Custom waveguide network approach addressing microring resonator power limits

metrics.other: identifies infeasible implementations due to power limits

limitations: Analysis focuses on tile-level communication; chip-level integration and manufacturing feasibility not detailed.
